methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a well-structured ML pipeline: feature selection via 100-bootstrap resampling, ridge-penalized Cox regression, Boruta, SHAP, ensemble with SVM+gradient boosting and a logistic-regression meta-learner, Bayesian hyperparameter search with five-fold CV, and explicit held-out test (20%) plus external validation on 8 public cohorts (n=1118). Multivariable Cox models with HR and 95% CI are reported, and restricted mean survival time loss ratios are used when proportional hazards are violated. Weaknesses include heterogeneous treatments across external cohorts (36.9% untreated), reliance on recomputed R-Oncotype DX/R-EndoPredict rather than the original proprietary algorithms, a noted sample-count inconsistency (1413 vs 1433 patients across text and figure), and some exploratory analyses (CDK4/6i drug screen in 5 cell lines) explicitly without multiplicity correction.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The assay addresses a real unmet need in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: detecting low-clinical-risk tumors at high recurrence risk who might benefit from adjuvant CDK4/6i. ER-Predict shows robust prognostic value (HR 2.03 DMFS in external validation), retains value in node-negative and stage I subsets, and outperforms recomputed multigene assays. However, as a retrospective development/validation using archival microarray data without prospective enrollment, the findings are hypothesis-generating for clinical decision-support and not yet evidence of impact on patient outcomes. Oxford LoE maps to 2b (retrospective cohort/prognostic validation).

reporting_quality.justification: As a prediction model study, TRIPOD is the applicable standard. The manuscript reports most TRIPOD items: predictor definition, outcome (DMFS), sample sizes, training/test split, internal and external validation, calibration in terms of survival functions, multivariable adjustment, comparison to established benchmarks, and a detailed limitations paragraph. Data sources are publicly identifiable (cBioPortal, GEO accession GSE6532, MetaGxBreast, DepMap, GDSC, Hartwig license HMF-DR-441), supporting moderate reproducibility, but no code repository or pre-registered protocol is referenced, and some figures/text disagree on sample counts (1413 vs 1433, 1118 vs 1128). TRIPOD items on model presentation (final weights/coefficients) and calibration plots are not fully addressed.

novelty_literature.justification: Multigene prognostic signatures in HR+/HER2- breast cancer are a mature field (Oncotype DX, MammaPrint, EndoPredict, PAM50) and these are explicitly cited and benchmarked. Novelty lies in the combination of a 14-gene ensemble ML model (linear SVM + gradient-boosted survival forest with logistic-regression meta-learner), demonstrated independent prognostic value when adjusted for R-Oncotype DX and R-EndoPredict simultaneously, robust signal for late (>5 year) recurrences where competitors weaken, and preliminary evidence for specificity to luminal endocrine-resistant biology with retained RB1. This is a meaningful novel combination/extension rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally well-written with a clear Introduction, well-structured Methods detailing the ML pipeline, and a thorough limitations section. Figures 1–4 logically trace development, external validation, benchmarking, and mechanism. Minor issues include a typo ('Notthingam'), occasional awkward phrasing ('ER-Predict is a leverages 14 genes'), repeated bullet points in the abstract area, and inconsistent cohort counts (1413/1433 and 1118/1128) that the reader must reconcile. Figure legends are detailed and mostly sufficient.

key_strengths: Robust ML pipeline with bootstrap feature selection, SHAP, ensemble classifier with meta-learner, Bayesian CV, and explicit internal + external validation on eight public cohorts (n=1118)
Independent prognostic value of ER-Predict over recomputed Oncotype DX and EndoPredict in multivariable models (HR 1.69, P<0.001) and specifically for late recurrences beyond 5 years
Biologically interpretable signal: enrichment for E2F targets and G2/M checkpoint with retained RB1 expression, supporting a candidate predictive niche for CDK4/6i
Extension to metastatic HR+ cohort on CDK4/6i (Hartwig, n=85) and cell line drug-sensitivity corroboration
key_concerns: Benchmark against recomputed Oncotype DX/EndoPredict rather than proprietary originals; the pipeline itself is not formally validated, as acknowledged
External cohorts are heterogeneous with 36.9% untreated and limited treatment annotation, and menopausal status is unavailable, limiting generalizability
Cohort count inconsistencies across text and figures (1413/1433 development; 1118/1128 external) raise confidence-in-reporting concerns
CDK4/6i-response claim rests on only 5 HR+ cell lines and 85 metastatic patients, and the predictive-for-CDK4/6i hypothesis is not formally tested prospectively
Model coefficients/weights are not presented; full reproducibility would benefit from a public code release
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid ML prognostic biomarker study with meaningful external validation and benchmarking, addressing an active clinical question around CDK4/6i patient selection; tier 2 acceptability with minor revisions to reconcile cohort counts and clarify TRIPOD/code-sharing items.
